Hi everyone,
I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.
We reached this decision after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.
If you would like to talk 1:1 this week, reply here and I will make time.
Thank you,
Leonard", "channel": "C0ADGSZKR3R", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"}]}

I will break down why and how to Push it to the low end.\\nI am not your lawyer or accountant, so treat this as planning guidance and sanity check, not formal advice.\\n\\n1. What drives the cost\\nKey factors that matter for Harmony Games specifically:\\n1. *Type of company and complexity*\\n    \\u25e6 Delaware C-corp with investors and a real cap table.\\n    \\u25e6 Multiple SAFEs / equity holders.\\n    \\u25e6 Employment / contractor agreements across countries.\\n    \\u25e6 Multiple commercial contracts (publishers, ad networks, platforms, vendors).\\n2. More complexity pushes you away from \\u201csimple startup dissolution\\u201d pricing and into custom work.\\n3. *Where fees show up*\\n4.  You are not just paying for \\u201cfile a dissolution form\\u201d:\\n    \\u25e6 corporate / securities law work.\\n    \\u25e6 Contract review and termination.\\n    \\u25e6 Employment and IP issues.\\n    \\u25e6 Tax and accounting cleanup.\\n    \\u25e6 Possibly some board / investor process work (consents, releases, etc.).\\n5. *Your goal*\\n    \\u25e6 If you want a \\u201cclean, defendable shutdown\\u201d that future investors and acquirers will not side-eye, you will spend more than the absolute bare minimum.\\n    \\u25e6 If you are ok with more \\u201cduct tape,\\u201d you can cut costs, but you increase risk of something biting you later.\\n2. Rough fee ranges by category\\nThese are order-of-magnitude numbers for a company like yours, using a mix of decent startup counsel + a scrappy accountant, not BigLaw overkill.\\nA. corporate dissolution & governance: *10k\\u201330k*\\nCovers things like:\\n\\u2022 Board and stockholder approvals.\\n\\u2022 Formal dissolution with Delaware, plus any foreign registrations (e.g. NC, CA, WA).\\n\\u2022 Handling investor rights, preference stack, and confirming There is no distribution or a small pro-rata distribution.\\n\\u2022 Drafting or reviewing:\\n    \\u25e6 Plan of liquidation / dissolution.\\n    \\u25e6 Officer certificates.\\n    \\u25e6 Releases and indemnities where needed.\\nIf everything is organized and you work with current counsel efficiently, you might land around *10k\\u201315k*. If lots of custom questions, messy history, or negotiations, *20k\\u201330k*.\\nB. Contracts, IP, and \\u201cshutting the business off\\u201d: *5k\\u201320k*\\nIncludes:\\n\\u2022 Reviewing and terminating:\\n    \\u25e6 publishing deals (Boombit, CrazyGames, etc.).\\n    \\u25e6 Platform agreements ([ORG_NAME_0308], IronSource, ad networks).\\n    \\u25e6 Vendor and contractor agreements.\\n\\u2022 Cleaning up IP:\\n    \\u25e6 Making sure all game code and assets are properly assigned to the company, so There is no surprise claim later.\\n    \\u25e6 Deciding what happens to IP: kept in the entity that will be dissolved, sold, or assigned to founders or a new entity.\\n\\u2022 Dealing with licenses (engine, SDKs) and privacy / data issues.\\nIf you have reasonably standard contracts and you are willing to send most termination notices yourself, lawyer time can be *5k\\u201310k*. If There is negotiation, disputes, or an IP transfer / sale, *15k\\u201320k+* is possible.\\nC. I will break down why and how to Push it to the low end.
I am not your lawyer or accountant, so treat this as planning guidance and sanity check, not formal advice.

1. What drives the cost
Key factors that matter for Harmony Games specifically:
1. *Type of company and complexity*
    ◦ Delaware C-corp with investors and a real cap table.
    ◦ Multiple SAFEs / equity holders.
    ◦ Employment / contractor agreements across countries.
    ◦ Multiple commercial contracts (publishers, ad networks, platforms, vendors).
2. More complexity pushes you away from “simple startup dissolution” pricing and into custom work.
3. *Where fees show up*
4.  You are not just paying for “file a dissolution form”:
    ◦ corporate / securities law work.
    ◦ Contract review and termination.
    ◦ Employment and IP issues.
    ◦ Tax and accounting cleanup.
    ◦ Possibly some board / investor process work (consents, releases, etc.).
5. *Your goal*
    ◦ If you want a “clean, defendable shutdown” that future investors and acquirers will not side-eye, you will spend more than the absolute bare minimum.
    ◦ If you are ok with more “duct tape,” you can cut costs, but you increase risk of something biting you later.
2. Rough fee ranges by category
These are order-of-magnitude numbers for a company like yours, using a mix of decent startup counsel + a scrappy accountant, not BigLaw overkill.
A. corporate dissolution & governance: *10k–30k*
Covers things like:
• Board and stockholder approvals.
• Formal dissolution with Delaware, plus any foreign registrations (e.g. NC, CA, WA).
• Handling investor rights, preference stack, and confirming There is no distribution or a small pro-rata distribution.
• Drafting or reviewing:
    ◦ Plan of liquidation / dissolution.
    ◦ Officer certificates.
    ◦ Releases and indemnities where needed.
If everything is organized and you work with current counsel efficiently, you might land around *10k–15k*. If lots of custom questions, messy history, or negotiations, *20k–30k*.
B. Contracts, IP, and “shutting the business off”: *5k–20k*
Includes:
• Reviewing and terminating:
    ◦ publishing deals (Boombit, CrazyGames, etc.).
    ◦ Platform agreements ([ORG_NAME_0308], IronSource, ad networks).
    ◦ Vendor and contractor agreements.
• Cleaning up IP:
    ◦ Making sure all game code and assets are properly assigned to the company, so There is no surprise claim later.
    ◦ Deciding what happens to IP: kept in the entity that will be dissolved, sold, or assigned to founders or a new entity.
• Dealing with licenses (engine, SDKs) and privacy / data issues.
If you have reasonably standard contracts and you are willing to send most termination notices yourself, lawyer time can be *5k–10k*. If There is negotiation, disputes, or an IP transfer / sale, *15k–20k+* is possible.
C. Employment, severance, and international wrinkles: *5k–20k*
You have:
• At least one US employee (WA).
• Contractors or employees in Turkey / Balkans / El Salvador, etc.
Items:
• Drafting or reviewing separation/severance agreements.
• Making sure state and country-specific rules are respected (notice, unused PTO, local labor rules).
• Confirming There are no outstanding claims or obvious liabilities.
If headcount is small and fairly aligned and you keep severance simple, legal review might be *5k–10k*. If you need local counsel in multiple countries or any disputes, *15k–20k+*.
D. Tax, accounting, and filings (non-legal): *5k–15k*
This is not legal fees but you have to budget it together:
• Final federal and state Tax returns.
• Sales tax / VAT cleanups if relevant.
• Final payroll / 1099s / T4s / foreign equivalents.
• Closing books, documenting treatment of remaining assets and liabilities.
A lean setup with a good startup CPA who already knows your books might be *5k–8k*. If There is multi-state, multi-country complexity and messy historical books, *10k–15k+*.
E. Contingency and “stuff you didn’t think of”: *5k–10k*
Even with good planning you will get:
• Extra questions from investors.
• A weird contract clause someone finds late.
• A platform or partner who needs a custom letter.
Having *5k–10k* in reserve avoids getting stuck mid-process.

3. Putting it together
For a harmonygames-like profile (Delaware C-corp, external investors, small global team, several commercial agreements, no massive litigation):
• *Very lean scenario, disciplined, everything clean:*
    ◦ Legal: 15k–25k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 5k–8k
    ◦ Contingency: 5k
    ◦ *Total: ~25k–38k*
• *More realistic “not perfect but not a mess” scenario:*
    ◦ Legal: 25k–45k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 8k–12k
    ◦ Contingency: 5k–10k
    ◦ *Total: ~38k–67k*
• *If things are messy or negotiated (IP sale, disputes, local counsel in multiple countries):*
    ◦ Legal: 40k–70k
    ◦ accounting / tax: 10k–15k
    ◦ Contingency: 10k
    ◦ *Total: ~60k–95k*
If you want a single planning number, I would assume *50k all-in* as a defensible budget, then work aggressively to drive it down.

4. How to Push toward the low end
If you decide to seriously plan for this, concrete things you can do now so fees do not explode:
1. *Organize everything:*
    ◦ Clean cap table and stock / SAFE docs in one folder.
• All major contracts in one spreadsheet with:
        ▪︎ Counterparty
        ▪︎ Term / termination clause
    ◦ Notice period
    ◦ Employment / contractor agreements and any option grants clearly filed.
2. *Standardize the exit pattern:*
• Decide in advance:
        ▪︎ Severance formula, if any.
        ▪︎ End dates and communication plan.
    ◦ What happens to IP.
    ◦ Then ask counsel to just “paper this plan,” not design it from scratch.
3. *Have existing counsel give a scoped quote:*
• Ask for:
        ▪︎ A fixed or capped fee for core dissolution package.
    ◦ Hourly for “extras” like complex negotiations or IP sale.
    ◦ Get at least one alternative quote from a smaller startup firm.
4. *Do founder work where possible:*
    ◦ Draft first pass of partner termination emails.
    ◦ Fill out standard forms where allowed.
    ◦ Only loop counsel for review and the parts that carry legal risk.
5. What I would actually do in your shoes
If you are purely planning, not pulling the plug:
• Mentally earmark *50k* as “shutdown runway” in your long-range model.
• In the next quiet window, email current counsel something like:
    ◦ “If we needed to do an orderly dissolution with no contentious issues and minimal distributions, roughly what ballpark would you expect in fees, and what can we do now to make that lower?”
• Make sure your books and cap table are clean enough that you can actually execute a shutdown without a 3-month archaeology project.

Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.

• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements

• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.

• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.

The wind-down channel confirms subscriptions were being triaged, and Metabase/dbt (~$300/mo) is being kept alive specifically for Combo Fighter data and moved to a personal card. Now let me pull the real Combo Fighter numbers from the warehouse and find the data-deal dollar figure. Let me first confirm exact game naming and date ranges.

SELECT game, MIN(date) AS first_day, MAX(date) AS last_day, COUNT(*) AS days,
SUM(dau) AS sum_dau, SUM(new_users) AS sum_new, SUM(returning_users) AS sum_ret
FROM ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS
GROUP BY game ORDER BY game

input.sql:
SELECT MIN(date) first_day, MAX(date) last_day, COUNT(DISTINCT date) days,
SUM(new_users) total_new_users, SUM(dau) sum_dau, MAX(dau) peak_dau,
SUM(total_sessions) total_sessions, ROUND(AVG(avg_session_minutes),1) avg_session_min,

content.text: Big finding: Combo Fighter's paid UA kept running at full pace **after** the Feb 9 shutdown — ~$2.4K more spent Feb 10–28 across six ad networks, and the campaigns are still live on the last data day. Let me quantify pre/post-shutdown spend precisely, confirm revenue, and check the "mostly organic" claim against install attribution.

input.sql:
SELECT
 SUM(CASE WHEN date <= '2026-02-09' THEN spend_usd ELSE 0 END) spend_thru_feb9,
 SUM(CASE WHEN date > '2026-02-09' THEN spend_usd ELSE 0 END) spend_after_feb9,
 SUM(CASE WHEN date <= '2026-02-09' THEN installs ELSE 0 END) inst_thru_feb9,
 SUM(CASE WHEN date > '2026-02-09' THEN installs ELSE 0 END) inst_after_feb9,
 SUM(spend_usd) total_spend, SUM(installs) total_installs,

import json,sys,re

        print("---")
EOF

input.title: Combo Fighter — Honest Post-Mortem & Wind-Down Financial Account (for angel calls)
input.body:
**Author:** Robert (Co-Founder / Creative Director)
**Date:** 2026-02-28
**Purpose:** A single, honest account of how Combo Fighter actually performed, what we paid to acquire its players, what is still costing us after the Feb 9 shutdown decision, and where the wind-down money genuinely leaves us. Written so Leonard has one straight source for the angel calls, and so the record outlasts our accounts going dark.
**Sources:** Snowflake (ANALYTICS + FINANCE warehouses) as the primary numbers; the wind-down Slack channel for the deal/settlement facts. Where the two disagree with numbers people pasted into threads, the warehouse wins.

---

## 1. Combo Fighter — what the data actually said

**Life of the game:** first day with players **2026-01-05**, last day with any player data **2026-02-09** (the shutdown day) — **36 days**. Paid-ad data runs to 2026-02-28 (see §2).

**Engagement (the genuinely good part):**
- Grew from ~45 DAU on day 1 to a peak of **~800 DAU** (Feb 7). ~845 new in-game players over the run; 55,101 total sessions.
- Solid daily habit while it lasted.

**Retention (honest, mixed):**
- **D1 ≈ 44%** (ranged 37–51% across the run). **D7 ≈ 22%. D30 ≈ 11%.**
- This is *better* than the "**D1 30%**" figure we reported to the board in January — the first-session hook was stronger than the number that has been circulating. But the D7→D30 decay (22% → 11%) is the real story: a strong hook that did not hold. Classic leaky mid-funnel.

**Monetization: $0.**
- Zero lifetime revenue. No IAP, no ad revenue, **0 paying users**. It never monetized — it stayed a prototype. So ARPU = 0, LTV = unknown, ROAS = 0.

**Cost to put players in front of it (real dollars, from the ad-spend ledger):**
- **Lifetime UA spend: $7,476** across **six networks** — Meta Facebook $2,265 · Meta Instagram $1,351 · Unity Ads $1,318 · Google UAC $1,068 · ironSource $742 · AppLovin $732.
- **1,341 paid installs · blended CPI $5.57.**
- Through the Feb 9 shutdown alone: **$5,035 spent / 898 installs.**
- Because revenue was $0, every dollar of that was sunk. **Effective ROAS = 0.**

**Two corrections to the story that's been circulating — because you asked me not to smooth it:**
1. **"Mostly organic" is not true by the money.** The attribution/MMP sample tells an organic-heavy, Facebook-only-paid story. The *spend ledger* shows a real, sustained, six-network paid campaign. Through Feb 9 there were ~898 paid installs against ~845 total new in-game players — i.e. growth was overwhelmingly **bought**. The hockey-stick DAU curve was paid acquisition, not virality.
2. **The board engagement headline was overstated.** The January deck cited ~55 min sessions. The warehouse shows average sessions ≈ **13 minutes**. (Retention was better than we told the board; session length was worse.)

**The honest one-line read:** Combo Fighter had a good first-session hook, retained a bit better than we said, but never held players past a week, never earned a cent, and its growth was paid — we spent ~$7.5K to learn there was no monetization and no organic pull. The data did say stop.

---

## 2. What is STILL quietly costing us after Feb 9

We decided to stop on the 9th and have been cancelling since, but the list was assembled fast. Two things are still taking money:

### 2a. Combo Fighter paid UA is STILL LIVE (the un-named one)
The ad campaigns were never turned off. **$2,441 was spent Feb 10–28**, across all six networks, at **~$130/day**, and it was **still running on the last data day (Feb 28)**. Nobody flagged or cancelled these in the wind-down triage. This is real cash leaving daily on a dead product, and it is creating **fresh payables to the exact ad networks (AppLovin, Unity) we are trying to settle to zero**.

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Cash on hand (Feb 28) | **$2,500** |
| Data-licensing deal | $22,500 gross **− $11,700 charge = $10,800 net** |
| **Total available** | **≈ $13,300** |

| Item | Amount | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SVB credit-card debt | ~$10,000 | last explicit figure Oct 2025; card used since — confirm exact payoff |
| Combo Fighter live UA payable | ~$2.4K & growing ~$130/day | **until campaigns are killed** |
| AppLovin | Oct $4K reportedly paid Nov; fresh balance from live UA unknown | open |
| Unity Pro / Singular | targeting **$0** | unconfirmed in writing |

**The honest read:**
- **Only if** (a) Unity + Singular truly forgive to $0 in writing **and** (b) the Combo Fighter UA is killed today, the ~$13.3K available clears the ~$10K SVB card with a **thin ~$3K cushion** — i.e. roughly "close without cash out of pocket," as Leonard hoped, but *barely*.
- It does **not** fund the reserves counsel flagged — taxes, final payroll, chargebacks, contingency (counsel's "plan for pain" was ~$50K). **Orderly ≠ fully reserved.**
- If Unity/Singular don't forgive, or the UA keeps running, we go cash-negative — and Leonard, Arthur and I are personally on the hook.
- **Net:** this is break-even-at-best, not comfortable. The single biggest controllable variable is turning off the Combo Fighter campaigns now.

1. **$0 lifetime revenue on ~1,300 paid installs at $5.57 CPI (~$7.5K UA) — D1 ~44% but D30 ~11%.** The data-driven reason we stopped: a real six-network paid test returned zero and never held players past a week.

3. **One live leak found and being killed:** ~$130/day still flowing to Combo Fighter ads post-shutdown (~$2.4K since Feb 9), now being turned off.

*This page is the canonical record. A tracking item has been filed for the still-live costs; a summary was posted to Leonard and Arthur in the wind-down channel.*

input.description:
Tracking the costs still running on our side after the Feb 9 shutdown decision. Founders (Leonard, Arthur, Robert) are personally on the hook, so each item is named with a figure and an owner.

## 1. Combo Fighter paid UA — STILL LIVE (highest priority)
- Ad campaigns were never turned off after Feb 9. **$2,441 spent Feb 10–28**, ~**$130/day**, still running on the last data day (Feb 28).
- Live across all six networks: Meta Facebook, Meta Instagram, Unity Ads, Google UAC, ironSource, AppLovin (MMP: Singular).
- Real cash leaving daily on a dead product; also creates fresh payables to AppLovin/Unity — the exact vendors we're trying to settle to $0.
- **Figure:** ~$2.4K since shutdown, growing ~$130/day. **Owner:** unassigned → Arthur/Leonard to KILL all Combo Fighter campaigns immediately via the ad accounts / Singular, and confirm final network payables.

## 2. Metabase + dbt — kept for Combo Fighter data
- Deliberately retained "until Robert stops caring about Combo Fighter data"; moved to Arthur's personal KubLLC card.
- **Figure:** ~$300/mo. **Owner:** Arthur Blake. Action: set a hard stop date (Robert's analysis for the angel-call write-up is now done — can cancel).

## Watch items (confirm closed, not yet verified)
- Unity Pro & Singular: insolvency/termination letters sent — get written confirmation of $0 balance & cancellation.
- SVB credit card: pay off from data proceeds and close.
- Carta: renewal 8/15, tied to closed Chase account — confirm it can't charge.
- Gusto / Deel / Intuit: intentionally kept during shutdown.

Full context & lifetime numbers: Confluence "Combo Fighter — Honest Post-Mortem & Wind-Down Financial Account" (PROD space).

<@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> — I went back to the actual warehouse (not the thread screenshots) and wrote up one honest account of Combo Fighter + where the wind-down money really leaves us, so Leonard has a straight source for the angel calls. Full write-up in Confluence (PROD): *"Combo Fighter — Honest Post-Mortem & Wind-Down Financial Account."* Highlights:

*Combo Fighter, its whole life (Jan 5 – Feb 9):*
• $0 revenue, ever — no IAP, no ads, 0 paying users.
• We spent *$7,476 on UA across 6 networks* (1,341 installs, $5.57 CPI) — $5,035 of it before we pulled the plug. All sunk, ROAS 0.
• D1 ~44% (better than the 30% we told the board), but D7 22% → D30 11%. Good hook, didn't hold.
• Two corrections vs what's been circulating: it was *not* "mostly organic" — the growth was bought; and the ~55min sessions in the Jan deck were really ~13min.

*Still costing us after Feb 9 (this is the part that got assembled too fast):*
• :rotating_light: *Combo Fighter paid UA was never turned off.* ~$2,441 spent Feb 10–28, ~$130/day, still live on all 6 networks as of the 28th. Nobody cancelled it, and it's making fresh payables to AppLovin/Unity — the vendors we're settling to $0. Needs killing today.
• Metabase + dbt ~$300/mo — the one we knew about, on Arthur's KubLLC card, kept for my Combo Fighter data (that analysis is now done).
Filed as *ENG-2438* (assigned to Arthur, urgent).

*Does the data sale cover an orderly close?* Roughly, but only barely: ~$10.8K net from the data deal ($22.5K − $11.7K) + $2.5K cash ≈ $13.3K, against ~$10K SVB card + the growing UA leak. That's break-even-at-best *if* Unity + Singular actually forgive to $0 in writing and we kill the ads now. It does not cover the tax/payroll/chargeback reserves counsel flagged. We three are personally on the hook, so I'd rather we see this straight now than have it surface later.

Done. I went to the primary sources — the Snowflake warehouse for the numbers, the wind-down Slack channel for the deal and settlement facts — and treated the pasted screenshots as unreliable where they disagreed.

**What I filed:**
- **Confluence (PROD):** *"Combo Fighter — Honest Post-Mortem & Wind-Down Financial Account"* — the durable, canonical write-up for Leonard's angel calls.
- **Slack #wind-down (C0ADGSZKR3R):** posted the summary tagging Leonard and Arthur.
- **Linear ENG-2438** (Urgent, assigned to Arthur): tracker for what's still costing us.

**The three things that matter most, honestly:**

1. **Combo Fighter never earned a dollar, and its growth was bought, not organic.** $0 lifetime revenue; ~$7,476 of UA across six networks (1,341 installs at $5.57 CPI, $5,035 of it before Feb 9), all sunk. Two corrections to the circulating story: it was *not* "mostly organic" (paid installs ~898 vs 845 new players through Feb 9), and the ~55-min sessions in the board deck were really ~13 min. The one thing that read *better* than we told the board: D1 was ~44%, not 30% — but D7 22% → D30 11% is why "the data said stop" is true.

2. **A live leak nobody named:** the Combo Fighter ad campaigns were never turned off. ~$2,441 spent Feb 10–28, ~$130/day, still running on all six networks on the last data day — and it's building fresh payables to AppLovin and Unity, the exact vendors we're trying to settle to zero. (Plus the known ~$300/mo Metabase+dbt on Arthur's personal card, kept for my Combo Fighter analysis — which is now done.)

3. **The money is break-even at best, not the cushion you may have been carrying.** ~$10.8K net from the data deal ($22.5K − $11.7K) + $2.5K cash ≈ $13.3K, against ~$10K SVB card debt plus the growing UA leak. It clears the card *only if* Unity and Singular actually forgive to $0 in writing and we kill the ads now — and it does **not** fund the tax/payroll/chargeback reserves counsel flagged (~$50K "plan for pain").

**If I were making those calls, I'd lead with:** *"$0 revenue on ~1,300 paid installs at $5.57 CPI — D1 44% but D30 11%; the paid test returned nothing, so we stopped,"* and *"the data sale lets us close roughly cash-neutral with no distribution — ~$13K covering ~$10K of debt, nothing to spare."* Then, quietly to Leonard and Arthur (not the angels): the ~$130/day still leaking needs to be off today, or point #3 turns negative and it lands on the three of us.

One caveat to flag: the exact SVB payoff is anchored to the last explicit figure (~$10K, Oct 2025) — worth confirming the current balance before Leonard commits to "cash-neutral" on a call.
